sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test imports and checks
sections.what: Groups the checks for unit names, candidate ranking, source windows, research names and outcome labels, all using fixed text examples.
sections.why: Likely reason: these rules are the ones most likely to match the wrong project if they drift.
sections.watch_out: Some expectations reflect specific project decisions, so ask the owner before changing one.

summary: Automated tests for how research sources are matched to projects, how their text is cut, how search phrases are built, and how outcome labels are handled.
purpose: Checks that the research matching rules work as designed before they decide which sources are used.
why: Likely reason: matching the wrong project or unit would put wrong evidence into the report, so these rules are tested directly.
how: Runs fixed text examples through the matching, ranking, windowing, naming and outcome functions, and checks each expected result.
inputs: Fixed example text and search results written inside the file.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each test.
risks: Expected results encode specific matching decisions, so a change in behaviour fails tests that may still be correct.
debug: If a test fails, read which assertion failed and compare it with the matching function in researchSelection.ts or the namesProject check. Check whether the change was intended before updating the expectation.
